# Python file and callable reference

Generated by `python scripts/build_reference.py` from the first-party source. Use the [architecture guide](architecture.md#python-source-map) for callers and workflow ownership; use the [command reference](command-reference.md) to launch workflows. Do not execute library files individually.

Each entry gives the module explanation, local import links, external packages and public top-level signatures. Import links are static source declarations, including conditional imports. Runtime dispatch and dynamic imports require the implementation and execution receipts. Parameters are inputs. The accompanying source documentation describes the implementation and return value where documented. An absent description is an explicit documentation gap, not a claim that the function has no output. Return sites reproduce source expressions and link to each branch. They describe source structure. Links open the actual implementation, including validation and file-writing branches. Dynamic logical namespaces in `configs/core_source_layout.json` can expose functions from consolidated files; use the namespace imported by the caller rather than guessing from a physical filename.

Reviewed explanations can also come from the [maintained API notes](python-api-notes.md). Each note is checked against the definition’s full syntax tree before generation; a changed implementation requires its explanation to be reviewed.

Inventory: **265 Python files**, excluding vendored software and standalone tests; optional lab helpers and checks are included. `verification.py` is included because it is also a public verification entry point.

Description coverage: **2407 of 2739 public top-level definitions** have a source docstring or reviewed note; **332 remain undocumented**. This counts available explanations, not their scientific verification or runtime coverage. Methods, nested functions and private helpers are outside this count.

## bootstrap.py

[Read implementation](../bootstrap.py)

Stdlib-only setup: python3 bootstrap.py --install --profile base.
Writable environments and builds belong to external RESEARCH2_STATE_ROOT.

**Local imports** [core/native.py](../core/native.py).

**External imports** `packaging`.

## core/action_angle.py

[Read implementation](../core/action_angle.py)

Actions, angles, frequencies and explicit orbit-validity diagnostics.

Actions: (Jr,Jz,Jphi) in kpc km/s, angles radians, frequencies km/s/kpc.
Spherical quadrature is independent of AGAMA; axisymmetric Staeckel-fudge
uses the project's pinned AGAMA backend. General fields get orbit diagnostics
and unavailable invariant actions instead of invented conserved quantities.

**Local imports** [core/halos.py](../core/halos.py), [core/stream_common.py](../core/stream_common.py).

**Imported by** [core/native_stream_responses.py](../core/native_stream_responses.py), [core/stream/experiments.py](../core/stream/experiments.py), [core/stream/workflow.py](../core/stream/workflow.py), [core/streams.py](../core/streams.py), [optional_tests/lab.py](../optional_tests/lab.py), [verification.py](../verification.py).

<a id="core-analysis-py"></a>
## core/analysis.py

[Read implementation](../core/analysis.py)

Saved-snapshot scientific measurements, catalogue statistics and publication.

Readers validate complete snapshot sets and their stored unit/epoch contracts.
Selected products publish immutable HDF5/figure bundles; the legacy full suite
retains its separate entry point. Numerical arrays, support masks and missing
measurements are authoritative; plots do not supply absent physics.
See docs/architecture.md for the pipeline and docs/calculations.md for equations.

<a id="core-apertures-py"></a>
## core/apertures.py

[Read implementation](../core/apertures.py)

Measured native selection apertures and their contamination histories.

Catalogue cohorts define mass-centered bounding spheres. Encounter spheres use
actual saved stellar positions and the declared search radius, preserving the
separate reconstructed event time. Centers are original-box comoving kpc/h;
radii are proper kpc, with x_comoving = x_proper*h/a before periodic wrapping.
Each aperture is measured separately: overlaps are not added into a union.
Missing ancestry, uncertain classification and unresolved events stay explicit.

## core/assembly.py

[Read implementation](../core/assembly.py)

Native halo/galaxy assembly, orbital events, workflow stages and figures.

Histories follow exact native ancestry and retain gaps in saved observations.
Masses use Msun, times Myr, radii proper kpc and velocities km/s; scale factor
and d ln(M)/d ln(a) are dimensionless. Event and transition estimates remain
conditional on the saved cadence, measurement masks and supplied fit errors.

## core/bao.py

[Read implementation](../core/bao.py)

BAO catalogue measurements, template fits and published compressed likelihoods.

Positions use comoving Mpc without h in an explicitly authored fiducial geometry.
alpha_perp=(DM/rd)/(DM/rd)_fid and alpha_parallel=(DH/rd)/(DH/rd)_fid.
Uncalibrated ratios do not identify H0. Conditional fits retain their fixed
background/drag-scale assumptions; optional reconstruction/pair/sampler engines
load only when selected. Reference: DESI 2024 III, arXiv:2404.03000.

<a id="core-baryon_products-py"></a>
## core/baryon_products.py

[Read implementation](../core/baryon_products.py)

Measured native gas, stellar-return, metal and population products.

All products reuse the saved hydro census and original physical units. Gas
histograms sum mass per physical bin; SFR is a whole-snapshot sum in Msun/yr.
Stellar source losses and gas recipient gains remain separate signed ledgers.
Stellar birth-metal bookkeeping is distinct from current gas metal inventory.
Population colors use summed spectral luminosities and the pinned SSP model;
incomplete coverage stays masked rather than becoming a whole-census total.

calibration, covariance, selection or posterior samples.

<a id="core-expansion_products-py"></a>
## core/expansion_products.py

[Read implementation](../core/expansion_products.py)

Post-fit expansion recovery, explicit domain decisions and original figures.

H0 and H(z) retain separate observable identities and km/s/Mpc units. Repeated
observers within one native realization form one statistical group. Recovery
truth is accessed only after estimator products are frozen. Execution success
and a declared domain's scientific acceptance remain separate.

## core/first_stars.py

[Read implementation](../core/first_stars.py)

Native first-cooling/birth analysis and resolved-cloud products.

Cooling uses recorded radiative losses, not temperature decline alone. Jeans
support uses proper density, temperature and measured smoothing; effective-EOS
or missing chemistry cannot establish primordial fragmentation or an IMF.
Births retain exact gas-parent/host ancestry and saved proper-time brackets.

<a id="core-gravity_fields-py"></a>
## core/gravity_fields.py

[Read implementation](../core/gravity_fields.py)

Host motion, reconstructed fields and extended gravity components.

Hermite motion uses recorded proper velocities. Proper cosmological center
velocities must include Hubble motion before entering this interface. Forces
are evaluated in the inertial frame, avoiding omitted fictitious forces.

Fields return Phi [(km/s)^2], acceleration [(km/s)^2/proper kpc], and
the potential Hessian [(km/s)^2/proper kpc^2]; the tidal tensor is -H(Phi).

**Local imports** [core/halos.py](../core/halos.py), [core/stream/trajectories.py](../core/stream/trajectories.py), [core/stream_common.py](../core/stream_common.py).

**Imported by** [core/matched_perturber_figures.py](../core/matched_perturber_figures.py), [core/sidm.py](../core/sidm.py), [core/stream/encounters.py](../core/stream/encounters.py), [core/stream/experiments.py](../core/stream/experiments.py), [core/stream/workflow.py](../core/stream/workflow.py), [core/streams.py](../core/streams.py).

**External imports** `numpy`, `scipy`.

| Public definition and input signature | Implementation / result description | Explicit return sites |
|---|---|---|
| [`HostFrame (class)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L30) | Move between measured body coordinates and a common inertial frame. Positions are proper kpc, velocities km/s and times Myr. R maps column body vectors into inertial vectors. For the row arrays used here, x_inertial = x_body R.T + center and v_inertial = (v_body + omega_body cross x_body / K) R.T + center_velocity, where K converts km/s to kpc/Myr. The rotation term is essential even when the body's origin is stationary. | Class. Inspect its methods and constructor. |
| [`SatelliteWorldline (class)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L90) | Recorded extended Plummer perturber; no inferred point-mass substitute. | Class. Inspect its methods and constructor. |
| [`TimeDependentHost (class)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L122) | Interpolate measured body-frame fields, then return inertial forces. Forces and Hessians transform as a_global = R a_body and H_global = R H_body R.T. Integrating in the inertial frame avoids adding Coriolis/centrifugal terms. Temporal field interpolation is a declared approximation inside measured support, not a convergence certificate. | Class. Inspect its methods and constructor. |
| [`RadialProfile (class)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L221) | Measured enclosed mass with finite-mass exterior and declared inner core. A monotone cubic mass interpolant gives rho=M'/(4 pi r^2). The potential is computed from the same M, not an independently fitted NFW potential. The outer truncation is the last measured radius. Central extrapolation is permitted only via the explicit constant-density-core assumption. | Class. Inspect its methods and constructor. |
| [`EvolvingPerturber (class)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L324) | Interpolate actual epoch forces/potentials, preserving disruption flags. Each profile carries its own measured epoch mass, matched to the worldline. Interpolating potential, force and Hessian with the SAME weight retains their derivative relationships; zero-mass epochs contribute zero gravity. | Class. Inspect its methods and constructor. |
| [`DifferentiatedPotential (class)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L359) | Consistent scalar-field finite differences for analytic nonradial models. The derivative spacing is a recorded numerical parameter; it must receive independent refinement controls. It is never a softening length. The deformed Plummer bar is an imposed potential family; it is not a Ferrers density model or a guarantee of positive density at every radius. | Class. Inspect its methods and constructor. |
| [`ComponentField (class)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L454) | Combine named imposed gravity components with matching accounting records. Require each component’s gravity_count to equal one, known physical roles and no overlapping declared native source IDs. evaluate(x,t) adds each component’s potential [(km/s)^2], acceleration [(km/s)^2 per proper kpc] and potential Hessian [(km/s)^2 per proper kpc^2], validating aligned finite arrays. This evaluates an imposed field; it does not evolve live gravitating particles or prove undeclared source identities are distinct. | Class. Inspect its methods and constructor. |
| [`FrozenField (class)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L481) | Wrap a field at one finite epoch. Every evaluate(x,t) call delegates to the underlying field with that saved epoch, ignoring the requested time while retaining the original position queries and output units. This supplies a static diagnostic control without copying or re-evolving the component. | Class. Inspect its methods and constructor. |
| [`MassScaledField (class)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L486) | Explicit fixed-shape imposed-field mass scaling; live response separate. | Class. Inspect its methods and constructor. |
| [`FixedCenterHost (class)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L495) | Freeze only recorded host translation; keep deformation/orientation. Evaluating the translating host at shifted query coordinates gives a controlled no-reflex field without introducing a fictitious force. | Class. Inspect its methods and constructor. |
| [`construct_component_control(full, intervention)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L508) | Build a declared intervention on an existing ComponentField: keep the full field, retain selected components, subtract them, freeze selected epochs, fix translating-host centres, or scale selected masses by a positive nonunit multiplier. Validate distinct existing component names and operation-specific inputs, preserve accounting for retained components and reject an empty result. Return the original full field or a new composite wrapper; this constructs a counterfactual force model rather than running its trajectories. | <code>full</code> [line 512](../core/gravity_fields.py#L512)<br><code>ComponentField(selected, accounting={name: full.accounting&#91;name&#93; for name in selected})</code> [line 528](../core/gravity_fields.py#L528) |
| [`fourier_torque_diagnostics(position, acceleration, mass, radial_edges)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L531) | Bin particles by cylindrical radius and return mass-weighted cosine/sine moments for azimuthal modes m=1 through 4 plus actual total z torque sum m(x cross a)_z in Msun (km/s)^2. Validate aligned finite positions/accelerations/masses, nonnegative masses and increasing radial edges; include the final upper edge. Empty or zero-mass bins retain NaNs and false support. Moments diagnose asymmetry; resonance identification requires separate orbital frequencies. | <code>{&#x27;fourier_m1_m4&#x27;: harmonic, &#x27;torque_z_msun_kms2&#x27;: torque, &#x27;fourier_supported&#x27;: support, &#x27;interpretation&#x27;: &#x27;mass Fourier moments and actual z torque; resonances require orbital f...</code> [line 543](../core/gravity_fields.py#L543) |
| [`FlattenedLogPotential (class)`](../core/gravity_fields.py#L548) | Potential-axis model with an analytically implied Poisson density. q_phi is explicitly a potential flattening. The implied density generally has different radius-dependent axis ratios and can be negative for overly flat configurations. Such models are rejected in their declared domain. | Class. Inspect its methods and constructor. |

## core/hmf_campaign.py

[Read implementation](../core/hmf_campaign.py)

Standalone linear HMF predictions and reproducible cosmology screening.

Every epoch uses its own solver P(k), not a scale-independent growth rescaling.
Formula spread and cosmology outliers are selection diagnostics, not errors.

## core/hmf_fitting_functions.py

[Read implementation](../core/hmf_fitting_functions.py)

Additional, analysis-only HMF comparisons; never changes a simulation or old plot.

Equations: Murray, Power & Robotham 2013, arXiv:1306.6721v1, Table 1.
Reed07 coefficients follow Reed et al. 2007 eqs. 11-12 (ca=0.764,
c=1.08); see https://hmf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/_modules/hmf/mass_function/fitting_functions.html.
All fits here use FOF b=0.2. No SO mass conversion is attempted.

<a id="core-matched-py"></a>
## core/matched.py

[Read implementation](../core/matched.py)

Matched cosmology/object comparisons, population statistics and workflows.

Compare common Lagrangian identities with explicit non-h-scaled physical units.
Within-realization object scatter is distinct from independent-realization
covariance. WDM discreteness screens describe numerical reliability, not a
physical cutoff. EDE contrasts refer to background/linear-input differences;
this module does not introduce a nonlinear EDE field into Gadget.

Adjoints from MUSIC windows through potentials, sources and shared noise.

For real arrays the transpose preserves <w, F(x)> = <F.T(w), x>. Potentials
include supported ghost cells; source weights retain their actual hierarchy.

must be added on the SAME noise variables before covariance is evaluated.
No transpose or solver residual establishes a physical field-error bound.

or continuum boundary accuracy. Native operators load only when requested.

<a id="core-music-phases-py"></a>
## core/music/phases.py

[Read implementation](../core/music/phases.py)

Native MUSIC phase formats and explicit frozen/seeded model verification.

GRAFIC conversion preserves the selected sign, byte order and axes. Cache
encoding changes representation only. The two replay models have different
conditioning and must not substitute for one another; their source/seed/cache
bindings are checked before moment calculations consume the resulting model.

<a id="core-music-poisson-py"></a>
## core/music/poisson.py

[Read implementation](../core/music/poisson.py)

Coupled MUSIC Poisson equations, independent references and failure intake.

The coupled operator keeps leaf source equations and eight-child restriction
rows distinct. Whole-box Fourier and rational failed-field calculations keep
independent arithmetic: sharing production stencils would hide disagreement.
All coordinates here use the declared normalized box, not implicit kpc units.
Linear residuals and model sensitivity are not physical accuracy certificates.

<a id="core-music-precision-py"></a>
## core/music/precision.py

[Read implementation](../core/music/precision.py)

Exact binary128 storage and its explicit native arithmetic adapter.

Retained fields stay as IEEE754 integer word pairs. NumPy longdouble is not
assumed to represent binary128, and there is no implicit float conversion or
precision fallback. The native reference builds only when its caller asks for
wide-field arithmetic; its derivative observables round to binary64 at output.

Signed physical transfers, Fourier refinement and gradients use the declared
native conventions. Captured sources/potentials are comparison inputs only
where explicitly stated. Discrete agreement does not establish continuum
accuracy, physical boundary conditions or a new statistical noise model.

<a id="core-music-seeded-py"></a>
## core/music/seeded.py

[Read implementation](../core/music/seeded.py)

MUSIC local seeded refinement, GSL replay and fixed-prefix moments.

The retained prefix is fixed. Subsequent raw tiles carry the declared global
mt19937 seeds and native Gaussian draws. Rectangular cache footprints preserve
periodic coordinates and inherited DC; they are not independent full cubes.
Moment calculation streams one observable at a time and accumulates a Gram
matrix on disk. Importing this module never loads GSL or draws a field.

<a id="core-music-windows-py"></a>
## core/music/windows.py

[Read implementation](../core/music/windows.py)

Finite MUSIC particle-window measurements and their native input responses.

A window selects particles in the original Lagrangian frame. Density modes
are dimensionless; velocity divergence uses km/s per comoving kpc/h. Responses
follow the actual source hierarchy, retained potentials and padded caches.
Their agreement alone establishes neither a noise covariance nor physical
boundary accuracy; those require the separate declared model and controls.

<a id="core-observation_geometry-py"></a>
## core/observation_geometry.py

[Read implementation](../core/observation_geometry.py)

Native observation geometry, stellar attenuation and survey measurements.

Readers preserve native identities and explicit per-epoch unit conversions.
Lightcones use no-h comoving distances and proper emission clocks. Lens planes
use proper kpc and Msun; their angular deflections are radians. Dark gravitating
mass does not acquire stellar light, and thin lenses do not model strong-field
black-hole ray tracing. Periodic replicas are not independent realizations.

## core/research/__init__.py

[Read implementation](../core/research/__init__.py)

Research workflows and measurements, grouped by responsibility.

capabilities: declared models, native settings and saved workflow inputs.
generator_controls: explicitly invoked MUSIC transfer and mixed-fluid checks.
controls: physical control inputs, build flags and measured native controls.
convergence: controlled variants, native input authority and paired comparisons.
measurements: native observables, history reductions and ensemble collection.
errors: correlated uncertainties, systematic envelopes and bounded refinement.
display: measured figures, graph galleries and native scene attachments.
restarts: exact native state, physical outputs and lifecycle comparisons.
checkpoints: coherent restart markers, retained copies and continuation policy.
zooms: parent material, descendant recovery and measured region adequacy.
pilots: representative campaigns, native populations and measured artifacts.
release: explicitly requested portable-build/restart/scene controls.
findings: optional failure history and supplied rerun measurements.

Shared units and simulation physics remain in their owning core modules.
Importing this package launches no work.

<a id="core-research-capabilities-py"></a>
## core/research/capabilities.py

[Read implementation](../core/research/capabilities.py)

Decide which workflows their declared physics and saved inputs can support.

Build support requires the recorded executable, compile options and input
fields. Saved-run selection checks actual particle species, epochs and fields.
These checks establish input availability; they do not establish accuracy or
convergence of the underlying physical model.

## core/research/checkpoints.py

[Read implementation](../core/research/checkpoints.py)

Publish restart markers from coherent native rank checkpoint generations.

Uses the existing GADGET CRC/layout/clock readers. Merely finding restart files
or waiting a fixed duration never establishes that a checkpoint is complete.

<a id="core-research-display-py"></a>
## core/research/display.py

[Read implementation](../core/research/display.py)

Assemble measured displays, graph galleries and native scene attachments.

The source arrays keep their measured units, identities, epochs and support.
Only scene adapters convert proper kpc to comoving Mpc/h, using h/(1000*a).
Periodic copies show the same physical selection; they add no physical mass.

<a id="core-research-findings-py"></a>
## core/research/findings.py

[Read implementation](../core/research/findings.py)

Optional history of reported failures and the measurements used to resolve them.

A fix can affect downstream products. This module follows those recorded
dependencies and checks supplied rerun results; a closed issue is not proof
that an entire simulation or physical model is accurate. Ordinary evolution
and analysis do not create this store automatically.

## core/research/restarts.py

[Read implementation](../core/research/restarts.py)

Compare retained native states before and after restart.

Physical observables carry explicit units and tolerances. Raw native members
retain their declared layouts and code units. Integer state and identities
compare exactly, including retired black holes and committed lifecycle events.

<a id="core-research-zooms-py"></a>
## core/research/zooms.py

[Read implementation](../core/research/zooms.py)

Prepare, recover and measure bounded native zoom campaigns.

Parent and zoom identities belong to different namespaces. Original MUSIC q
coordinates map parent-cell material to fine zoom representatives; evolved
IDs then locate descendants. Saved native epochs and measured contamination,
force errors and observables determine support for each requested history.

peak usage. Scientific dependencies are imported only by the census/estimators
that need them; basic resource discovery also works in portable Blender Python.

<a id="core-sidm_physics-py"></a>
## core/sidm_physics.py

[Read implementation](../core/sidm_physics.py)

Elastic SIDM angular models, native tables and explicit engine parameters.

Relative speeds are km/s. Differential cross sections are d(sigma/m)/dOmega
in cm^2/g/sr, with mu=cos(theta) on [-1,1] and azimuthal measure 2*pi.
Total, ordinary-transfer, identical-particle modified-transfer and viscosity
moments remain distinct. Folded identical-particle angles use |mu| on [0,1].
Nonlinear scattering settings do not replace the linear cosmological transfer
model. Table preparation computes model inputs; it does not evolve particles
or establish numerical convergence.

<a id="core-sidm_products-py"></a>
## core/sidm_products.py

[Read implementation](../core/sidm_products.py)

SIDM history, matched contrasts, derived figures and campaign export routes.

Use measured native histories, their physical units and original support masks.
A branch contrast is delta Q = Q_branch - Q_baseline. The dimensionless plotted
contrast is delta Q / max(abs(Q_baseline), the declared dimensional floor),
not a branch/baseline ratio. Paired differences alone do not give independent
ensemble covariance, and a density rise alone does not prove core collapse.
Native evolution lives outside this module; these reducers use saved native
measurements and export their scientific figures.

ambiguous recovery remains unresolved; genuine ingestion/accounting errors
still raise and stop the workflow with their original evidence.

<a id="core-stellar_observations-py"></a>
## core/stellar_observations.py

[Read implementation](../core/stellar_observations.py)

Stellar observation models: spectral-age chronometers and distance ladders.

Native SSP particles provide host populations, not resolved Cepheid pulsations
or SN explosions. Indicator prescriptions and generating/fitting spectral assets
remain explicit. Ages are Gyr, wavelengths Angstrom, magnitudes in the authored
photometric system; distances are physical Mpc without h. Estimators do not read
native formation-age or H0 truth. References: Moresco arXiv:2003.07362; SH0ES
arXiv:2112.04510; Pantheon+ arXiv:2202.04077.

## core/stellar_population.py

[Read implementation](../core/stellar_population.py)

Native stellar/gas history intake and pinned FSPS population synthesis.

Native clocks determine ages in Myr; synthesis takes ages in Gyr. Luminosities
scale with gross initially formed mass in Msun, not present surviving mass.
FSPS surviving mass and the simulation's locked/current masses remain distinct.
Unavailable model-domain coverage stays masked; no age/metallicity clipping.

## core/stream/experiments.py

[Read implementation](../core/stream/experiments.py)

Physical stream experiments, selection and campaign stage dispatch.

Coordinates are proper kpc, velocities km/s and clocks Myr in the declared
frame. Candidate rescaling is an explicit diagnostic model; it does not turn
an altered trajectory into a measured native orbit. Inference uses recorded
priors, selection normalization and real sampler products.

Missing coordinates are marginalized through covariance submatrices. Shape

per-object selection explicit. A written chain is not scientific acceptance.
Optional sampler backends load only when a fit is requested.

<a id="core-stream_resimulation-py"></a>
## core/stream_resimulation.py

[Read implementation](../core/stream_resimulation.py)

Live self-gravitating stellar stripping and calibrated release adapters.

The reference integrator is deterministic direct softened gravity in an
inertial frame, coupled to the actual time-dependent parent field. This supports
collisionless stellar systems; collisional clusters and DM-bearing SIDM systems
need a native physics engine. Particle spray is a distinct approximation.

Preflight estimates are separate from measured aperture counts and convergence.

## core/stream_tracks.py

[Read implementation](../core/stream_tracks.py)

Principal stream curves, transported frames and local observables.

No global RMS width substitutes for local transverse covariance. Crossing
tracks require phase-space or ancestry separation; unresolved forks are flagged.
Spline residuals are weighted by centroid uncertainty; the smoothing budget
is dimensionless. Geometry and local widths use the same fitted curve.

## optional_tests/advanced_controls.py

[Read implementation](../optional_tests/advanced_controls.py)

Regenerate known-shape, density-valley and flyby figures using production readers.

Run with the Research2 environment from any directory. Shapes uses 6000
particles; splashback uses 32768; orbits uses 32. These are authored HDF5 inputs, not evolved
or converged halos. No downloads, builds, movies or archives are created.
Missing dependencies report UNAVAILABLE; all generated files stay external.

<a id="optional_tests-lab-py"></a>
## optional_tests/lab.py

[Read implementation](../optional_tests/lab.py)

Run bounded, portable teaching experiments and preserve their numerical proof.

Usage: python optional_tests/lab.py run --particles 32 --output NEW_DIRECTORY
       python optional_tests/lab.py serve

Synthetic HDF5 fixtures are labeled and never certified as native evolution.
Core numerical functions perform the measurements. Each step records its
inputs, equations, implementation, assertions, artifacts and elapsed time.

## optional_tests/native_checks.py

[Read implementation](../optional_tests/native_checks.py)

Fixed native-package calculations for the optional lab, never installers.
